# Audio fixtures

The committed corpus every transcript-accuracy claim in this repository is
measured against. Constitution Principle II ("Transcript Accuracy Is Measured,
Not Asserted") requires a fixed, committed fixture set; this is it.

Consumed by `tests/transcription_fixtures.rs` via the helpers in
`tests/support/mod.rs`.

## Contents

| Fixture | Class | Duration | Speakers | Source | Licence | Reference transcript |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `silence-5s.wav` | non-speech | 5.0 s | 0 | Generated by `../generate.sh` | CC0 / public domain (synthesized, no copyrightable input) | none — expected empty |
| `noise-fan-10s.wav` | non-speech | 10.0 s | 0 | Generated by `../generate.sh` (seeded pink noise, low-passed) | CC0 / public domain | none — expected empty |
| `noise-keyboard-10s.wav` | non-speech | 10.0 s | 0 | Generated by `../generate.sh` (seeded gated white noise) | CC0 / public domain | none — expected empty |
| `music-10s.wav` | non-speech | 10.0 s | 0 | Generated by `../generate.sh` (sine triad) | CC0 / public domain | none — expected empty |

**Conversational speech fixtures are not yet present.** See "Adding speech
fixtures" below — this is a known, deliberate gap, not an oversight.

## Format contract

Every fixture is **16 kHz mono signed 16-bit PCM WAV**. The harness rejects
anything else rather than silently resampling it, because a fixture in the wrong
format measures a different pipeline than the one under test.

A fixture named `foo.wav` may have a sibling `foo.txt` holding its reference
transcript. A non-speech fixture has no `.txt`: its expected transcript is
empty, and the harness asserts emptiness rather than skipping.

## Why the harness Opus round-trips these

Discord delivers Opus at 48 kHz; songbird decodes it before the bot ever sees
PCM. A fixture fed to the recognizer as clean PCM measures a pipeline this bot
never runs — it would report accuracy the deployed system does not achieve, and
would hide any regression that lives in the codec path.

So the harness encodes each fixture to Opus at 48 kHz and decodes it back to
16 kHz mono before transcribing (`tests/support/opus_round_trip`). The files on
disk are clean; the audio the recognizer sees is not. See research.md R5.

## Reference transcript conventions

WER is meaningless unless the reference and the hypothesis are normalized the
same way. These rules are what make a reference reproducible by a second person:

- **Verbatim words only.** Write what is said, not what was meant.
- **Lowercase.** Comparison is case-insensitive, but write lowercase anyway so
  diffs are readable.
- **No punctuation** except apostrophes inside words (`don't`, `it's`).
- **Numbers spelled out** as spoken: "twenty twenty six", not "2026".
- **Disfluencies included** when clearly audible as words ("um", "uh"), omitted
  when they are non-lexical noise (breaths, lip smacks, laughter).
- **Unintelligible audio** marked `[unk]`, which the scorer counts as one token
  that nothing can match — so it costs exactly one error rather than being
  silently forgiven.
- **One line per fixture.** Newlines are collapsed to single spaces.

`tests/support::normalize_transcript` implements exactly this for the
hypothesis side. If you change the convention, change both.

## Accuracy tolerances

The numbers the harness is judged against. Stated here rather than left to
interpretation, because "transcripts agree" is not a testable claim:

| Comparison | Tolerance | Serves |
|---|---|---|
| Same backend, same fixture, repeated runs | exact match after normalization | determinism — greedy sampling is deterministic; divergence here is a defect |
| CPU vs GPU (accelerated variant), per fixture | **WER delta ≤ 0.02 absolute** (2 percentage points), and non-speech fixtures must be empty on **both** | feature 001, SC-003 |
| Non-speech fixture, any backend | normalized transcript must be **empty** | hallucination check |

The CPU/GPU tolerance is not zero because CUDA and CPU kernels accumulate
floating point in different orders; identical output is expected but not
guaranteed to the bit. A delta above 0.02 means the backend switch changed what
users read, which is a finding to investigate, not to widen the tolerance for.

## Regenerating

```sh
tests/fixtures/generate.sh
```

Regenerates only the synthesized non-speech fixtures, deterministically — a
re-run produces byte-identical files. Speech fixtures are never regenerated;
they are recordings.

## Adding speech fixtures

The WER baseline needs real recorded conversational speech. Synthesized speech
will not do: it is unrepresentative of what the recognizer actually faces, so a
WER measured against it would not predict production accuracy (research.md R5).

To add one:

1. Source a public-domain or CC0 conversational clip, 10-30 s. LibriVox
   (public domain) and Mozilla Common Voice (CC0) are both suitable; the licence
   must permit redistribution in this repository.
2. Convert it to the format contract above:
   ```sh
   ffmpeg -i source.ext -ar 16000 -ac 1 -c:a pcm_s16le tests/fixtures/audio/<name>.wav
   ```
3. Write `<name>.txt` by **listening to the clip** and transcribing it under the
   conventions above. Do not paste a transcript supplied by the source and do
   not accept a machine transcription — the reference is the ground truth the
   recognizer is scored against, so deriving it from a recognizer makes the
   measurement circular.
4. Add a row to the Contents table recording provenance, licence, speaker count
   and duration.
5. Run `cargo test --test transcription_fixtures` and record the resulting WER
   in the pull request.

Target: 3-5 clips. Keep the total corpus in the low single-digit megabytes —
this repository has no Git LFS, and R5 says plain git is the right choice at
that size.
